planNotes:
THE SHARED SOFT-CURRENCY BALANCE IS `currencies.Credits`. Every economy feature mutates that ONE number, and the integration gate must race them against each other:
- EARN: salvage (manual smelter collect + auto-collect tick), offline (away-accrual claim on join), daily (supply-drop reward), monetization (Credit pack S/M/L via ProcessReceipt).
- SPEND: structures (every catalog purchase), depth (each depth-unlock cost).
- RESET: resurface (sets Credits to 0, wipes upgrades, mints Pearls, ++resurfaces).
The second balance `currencies.Pearls` is minted ONLY by resurface and spent ONLY by structures (the Pearl-priced catalog entries) — the dupe surface named in the success criteria. Mandatory races for the integration gate: spam-duplicated `salvage.collect`; interleaved `structures.buy` + `depth.descend`; `resurface.do` duplicated in the same frame (Pearl dupe); `offline.claim` landing concurrently with a purchase; and `plot.claim` racing a leave->claim on a full server. ALL Credits/Pearls mutation must go through the contract pass's `ctx.economy` helper INSIDE a single `DataService:update` transform — never read-then-write across a yield.

ORDERING RATIONALE. The scaffold is empty (only the deletable `sample`), so batch 0 must stand the data shape up. `plot` is contract-defining and gives every later feature its per-player world root (`ctx.plot:rootFor`), so `salvage` (batch 1) parents the smelter/conveyor/drones under it — that real dependency is why the spec's "built with plot ownership" becomes two adjacent batches rather than one. `daily` and `leaderboard` join batch 0 because they have no feature dependency at all (daily grants Credits through `ctx.economy`; leaderboard only READS the contract-pass-provided `stats.lifetimeCredits`, so it must NOT be given a false dependency on the earn paths). `structures` (batch 2) follows salvage because its success criterion is a DELTA ON THE RUNNING RATE — it can only be proven against salvage's rate seam. `depth` needs both (hull rating from structures, the rate/value chain from salvage); `offline` needs salvage's rate + capacity. `resurface` and `monetization` land last because they modify what the earlier features already do.

DECISION 1 — WHO OWNS THE TICK. SalvageService owns ONE server-wide accrual loop (a single `task` loop over live sessions, not one loop per player), cadence ~1s on the injected server clock. Per tick, per session: `stored = math.min(capacity, stored + rateFor(data) * (now - smelter.lastTickUnix))`, then stamp `lastTickUnix = now`, all inside `DataService:update`. NOTHING else in the game runs a tick loop.

DECISION 2 — THE RATE IS A DERIVED FUNCTION, NEVER A PERSISTED FIELD. `ctx.salvage:rateFor(data) -> creditsPerSecond` is PURE over the persisted blob and is re-evaluated on every tick and every `salvage.fetch`. Its inputs: `upgrades.drones`, `upgrades.conveyor`, `upgrades.pearlDrones` (structures); `data.resurfaces` (permanent prestige multiplier); `data.flags["gamepass.doubleCredits"]` and `now < data.boostExpiresUnix` (monetization — read straight off the blob, so no seam and no race); and the per-tier + restock multiplier via the NIL-SAFE `ctx.depth:valueMultiplier(data, now)` seam. Salvage is built in batch 1 with all of those absent/zero and must still be correct; when the later features land they change the rate with ZERO edit to salvage. THIS IS THE PLAN'S #1 written-never-read risk: the integration gate must assert that a structures purchase, a depth descend, a resurface, the 2x gamepass, the 2x boost AND the restock each produce a measurable delta on the value `salvage.fetch` returns — no purchasable ships inert.

DECISION 3 — NO DOUBLE-COUNTING THE AWAY WINDOW. The window `[timestamps.lastSeenUnix, now]` belongs EXCLUSIVELY to OfflineService. SalvageService MUST stamp `smelter.lastTickUnix = now` at session load, before its first tick, so the online tick never re-counts it. Correspondingly the smelter TICK is not an earn: `stats.lifetimeCredits` and `currency_earned` fire when stored Credits are COLLECTED (manually or by auto-collect), never when they accrue into `smelter.storedCredits`.

DECISION 4 — RESTOCK IS OWNED BY `depth`. The daily rich wreck appears only in the re-entry-hooks bullet and would otherwise be orphaned. It "spawns in one trench tier" and its effect is a per-tier salvage-value multiplier, which is exactly what depth already owns — so it rides depth's single `valueMultiplier` seam instead of adding a second multiplier seam to salvage. Its day index comes from the server clock only.

DECISION 5 — THE PRESSURE GATE. Depth tier N requires (a) tier N-1 already unlocked, (b) `upgrades.hull >= HULL_MIN[N]`, and (c) enough Credits — all three checked against the SAME lock-held snapshot in which the Credits are debited. The ordinal requirement (b+c evaluated together, tiers strictly sequential) is what makes "cannot be bypassed by re-ordering purchases" true: buying hull first, or Credits first, or spamming descend, all converge on the same guarded transform.

MERGE HAZARD THE ORCHESTRATOR OWNS. Three files are EXPLICIT registries with one line per feature and will conflict on every union merge: `src/server/init.server.luau` (the deterministic services list), `src/client/init.client.luau` (the controllers list), and `tests/run.luau` (SPEC_PATHS). The contract pass should leave a clearly marked insertion block in each; the orchestrator resolves the merge. Feature builders must not reorder those lists — NetServer then DataService must stay first, and AnalyticsService + EconomyService must start before any feature service.

SCAFFOLD DEBT THE CONTRACT PASS MUST CLEAR FIRST. `Migrations.default` still seeds collect-sim's `currencies = { Stardust = 0 }`, and `data.spec` / `economy_race.spec` / `migration.spec` assert on `currencies.Stardust` in 30+ places. If that is not retargeted to Credits before fan-out, every Credits read starts nil and the gauntlet goes red mid-batch. Likewise `tests/lib/mocks.luau` passes only security/flags/analytics/monetization into the ActionContext — the new `economy` / `plot` / `salvage` / `depth` seams must be added there and to `Net.ActionContext` (a --!strict type error otherwise) or nine feature specs will each hand-roll their own ctx.

CLIENT JOIN RACE. This scaffold has no `src/client/framework/JoinRetry.luau` (collect-sim gained one only after the defect that lost offline earnings permanently). Every controller here fetches on Start — plot, salvage, offline and daily all read state that only exists after `loadSession` yields. The contract pass stands JoinRetry up as client framework and every controller must fetch through it. No offline rung can see this defect; it is a T2.7 finding by construction.

ORCHESTRATOR AMENDMENT A8 (assigns an unowned spec number). PACING TARGETS — spec line 26: "~90s to first Credits; first Depth unlock ~10-15 min". No feature slice can own this: salvage owns the base rate, structures its cost curve, depth its tier costs — three numeric tables built in three different batches, and only their COMPOSITION is the player's experience. It is therefore assigned to the INTEGRATION GATE as an explicit, COARSE assertion: from a fresh player at the starting structure set, time-to-first-Credits and time-to-afford-Depth-2 must both land inside a generous band around the spec's targets (an order-of-magnitude check, never a tuned equality). A composed result 10x off is a real defect no per-feature gate can see; the exact numbers are a human tuning judgment at the playtest, and the handoff note must say so rather than implying an offline rung tuned them.

ORCHESTRATOR AMENDMENT A11 (states owners the plan left implicit). The two WHOLE-GAME success criteria own no feature slice by design: "an integration test traverses claim->salvage->buy->descend->resurface and emits loop_completed" is owned by the integration-gate workflow, and "No open exploit — adversarial pass clean" is owned by the adversarial-review workflow. Recorded because an unstated owner for a literal success criterion is how a criterion goes unrun. NOTE FOR THE GATE: loop_completed fires at the FIRST successful descend, which is one step BEFORE the traversal's end — the traversal continues on to resurface, so the gate must observe the event at the descend and keep going, not expect it at the final step.

ORCHESTRATOR AMENDMENT A10 (contract-pass obligations no feature slice can own). Beyond the retrofits above: (e) `structures.fetch` MUST iterate the server-owned CATALOG, never the raw upgrades blob — the plan's own rationale for keeping timestamps out of the upgrades map depends on this, and enumerating the blob would expose upgrades.depth as purchasable. (f) Every service MUST register its actions as CLOSURES over service state inside Start(); the scaffold's SampleService registers a STATIC module table, which cannot reach service state — and offline's in-memory pending amount plus leaderboard's snapshot are exactly the state a static handler cannot see. Both are stated in the contract pass so nine builders do not each guess.

netActions.comment: [plot] claim a free dome. The payload carries NO plot id — the server picks; a client-named plot IS the plot-claim-hijack exploit. Second claim -> Err(Rejected); server full -> Err(Unavailable).
[plot] read which dome this player holds (id + world position) for the HUD/highlight. Must be JoinRetry-guarded on the client.
[salvage] empty the smelter: move smelter.storedCredits into currencies.Credits via ctx.economy:earn. Spam-duplicate safe (the second call finds 0 stored).
[salvage] read the DERIVED running income rate + stored + capacity. This is the observation surface the 'purchased structures change the income rate' criterion asserts a delta on.
[structures] server-validated purchase of one catalog entry (drones/conveyor/smelter/hull/pearlDrones); cost is server-derived, never sent by the client.
[structures] read the catalog with server-derived next-level prices + this player's levels, so the shop UI never holds its own price constants.
[depth] unlock + descend to the next trench tier. Pressure gate (prior tier + hull minimum + Credits) evaluated in the same lock-held transform that debits.
[depth] read current tier, the next tier's Credits + hull requirement, and TODAY's restock tier (the daily rich wreck) for the HUD badge.
[offline] claim the away-window accrual computed on the server from timestamps.lastSeenUnix. One-shot per session; no client-supplied time anywhere in the payload.
[daily] claim the supply drop; server-clock gated on the 20-22h window, Err(OnCooldown) before it opens.
[resurface] prestige: wipe structures + depth + Credits, mint Pearls, ++resurfaces. Err(PrereqUnmet) below the minimum depth. Duplicate-safe (no Pearl dupe).
[resurface] preview the Pearls that would be minted, the resulting permanent multiplier, and whether the minimum depth is met — so the confirm UI is server-truthed.

[leaderboard] read the current top-N snapshot by stats.lifetimeCredits. NOTE: monetization adds NO action — gamepass prompts are client-initiated MarketplaceService calls and product grants are server-driven through ProcessReceipt.

AMENDMENT A5 [offline] read the PENDING away-accrual grant (amount + whether it was capped) WITHOUT claiming it, so the claim-on-join popup can show it. The pending amount lives in server memory, not in PlayerData, so it is not in PlayerView and had no read surface at all. Peeking must be SIDE-EFFECT FREE: it never grants, never clears the pending amount, and never re-stamps the away window. JoinRetry-guarded on the client.

resultCodes.name: Insufficient
resultCodes.why: NOT PRESENT in this scaffold's Result.luau today (the file ships BadPayload/BadType/OutOfRange/NotOwner/RateLimited/UnknownAction/NoData/Internal/Rejected/SessionLocked/LockStolen/SessionClosed — Insufficient and OnCooldown exist only in collect-sim). Needed by every spend path: structures.buy, depth.descend, and salvage.collect on an empty smelter. Considered OutOfRange (a payload-range failure, not a balance state), Rejected (the global panic refusal), BadPayload.

resultCodes.name: OnCooldown
resultCodes.why: NOT PRESENT in this scaffold today. Needed for the daily supply-drop claim attempted before its 20-22h window opens. Considered RateLimited (that is the per-action token bucket the Gate enforces — conflating a 20-hour game cooldown with an anti-spam limit would make the daily-window test indistinguishable from a rate-limit test), Rejected, Insufficient.

resultCodes.name: PrereqUnmet
resultCodes.why: A NON-CURRENCY prerequisite is unmet: hull rating below the tier minimum, the previous tier not yet unlocked, the VIP-trench gamepass flag absent, or resurfacing below the minimum depth. Considered Insufficient (reserved for a currency shortfall — overloading it is exactly what would make the 'pressure gate holds' criterion untestable, because a hull-too-low refusal and a plain can't-afford refusal would be the same code), OutOfRange (payload range, not world state), NotOwner (acting player vs target owner), Rejected (the panic-flag refusal).

resultCodes.name: Unavailable
resultCodes.why: The resource exists but none is free right now: every dome plot on this server is already held, so the join claim cannot be satisfied. Considered NoData (means 'no record for this key', not 'all instances taken'), Rejected (reserved for the panic-flag global refusal AND used here for the second-claim case — reusing it for both would make 'a second claim is refused' and 'the server is full' indistinguishable in the exclusivity test), Insufficient (currency), Internal (implies a bug, this is a normal capacity state).

resultCodes.name: AlreadyClaimed
resultCodes.why: The plan refused a second plot claim with Rejected, but this spine already uses Rejected as the PANIC flag — Net.dispatch returns exactly Result.Codes.Rejected("client writes rejected (panic)") at Net.luau:152, and Result.luau:15 documents it as such. The success criterion "a second claim is refused" would then be byte-indistinguishable from "the server is panicked and refusing all client writes". Verified against the real scaffold before adding this code.

currencyKeys.why: The soft primary currency ('Currencies: Credits (soft, primary)'). Rides the OPEN currencies map — a new key needs NO migration. This is the SHARED balance salvage/offline/daily/monetization credit and structures/depth debit and resurface zeroes, i.e. the cross-feature contention the integration gate races. The contract pass must ALSO replace the scaffold's leftover `Stardust = 0` seed in Migrations.default with `Credits = 0`.

The prestige currency ('Pearls (prestige currency, from resurfacing)'). Rides the OPEN currencies map — a second currency is a new KEY, never a migration. Minted only by resurface; spent only on the Structures shop's Pearl-priced entries. Seeded to 0 in Migrations.default; an absent key reads as 0, so existing blobs need no step.

typesFields.why: Total Credits EARNED over the player's lifetime, monotonic, never decremented on spend and never reset by resurface — it is the leaderboard's ranking key. No seam carries it: currencies.Credits is the SPENT-DOWN balance and therefore cannot represent a lifetime total, and it must be incremented on earn paths that live inside OTHER features (salvage, offline, daily, monetization), so no feature builder can own it. It rides INSIDE the closed `stats` record, which toView copies wholesale — so it is client-facing with NO extra allowlist line, but adding it to a fixed-shape record is still a structural change and needs the v1->v2 step. AMENDMENT A4: PlayerView.stats is a NARROW fixed record — Types.luau:48 declares stats: { playtimeSeconds: number, joinCount: number }. toView copies data.stats wholesale so the VALUE arrives, but a client reading view.stats.lifetimeCredits is a --!strict property error, and the widened PlayerData.stats may not satisfy the narrower PlayerView.stats annotation. The contract pass MUST widen PlayerView.stats too — widening PlayerData.stats alone ships a leaderboard that cannot read its own ranking key.

A per-player OWNED-SLOT IDENTITY plus the server-clock stamp of when it was taken. currencies is numbers, flags is booleans, upgrades is purchased LEVELS (and is enumerated by the shop's fetch, so a plot id parked there would surface as a purchasable), receipts is an idempotency ledger — none can express a string identity paired with a timestamp. Needs its own toView line (top-level field).

The smelter's un-collected output plus the ACCRUAL TICK BASE. Two reasons no seam fits: (1) storedCredits is not a currency — it is not spendable and must never appear in the HUD's currency row or be debited by a purchase, so parking it in the currencies map corrupts the meaning of the shared balance; (2) lastTickUnix must be a stamp DISTINCT from timestamps.lastSeenUnix, because the data layer re-stamps lastSeenUnix on every autosave — using it as the online tick base would silently zero the accrual window on each autosave (the known offline-base re-stamping defect class). upgrades is {[string]: number} and could physically hold both, but it is the shop's purchased-level map and is enumerated by structures.fetch. Needs its own toView line.

A streak count paired with a server-unix claim stamp. flags is boolean-only. upgrades could physically store two numbers, but it is the shop's purchased-level map — structures.fetch enumerates its keys, so a lastClaimUnix parked there would render as an upgrade with level 1754400000 and could be 'bought'. A fixed-shape record with its own migration step is the honest home. Client-facing: the HUD badge shows the streak. Needs its own toView line.

The PRESTIGE COUNT ('reset structures for Pearls + a permanent multiplier; count persisted'). currencies.Pearls cannot represent it: Pearls are spent on Pearl-only drones, so the spent-down balance would shrink the permanent multiplier every time the player shops. upgrades is wiped BY the resurface itself, so the count cannot live there. A top-level number with its own step + toView line.

Server-unix expiry of the 30-min 2x boost; 0 = none. The spec demands it be PERSISTED ('the expiry survives a crash/rejoin, not session-only'). flags is boolean (cannot hold an expiry), receipts is the boolean idempotency ledger, currencies would make it spendable, upgrades would render it as a purchasable level. A top-level number with its own step + toView line, read by salvage's rateFor as `now < boostExpiresUnix`.

Purchased COUNT of salvage drones. Rides the open upgrades map — NO Types edit and NO migration. Registered here only so structures (writer) and salvage's rateFor (reader) agree on the exact key spelling across parallel builds.
Purchased conveyor-speed level. Open map, no migration. Canonical key so salvage's rateFor reads what structures writes.
Purchased smelter-capacity level. Open map, no migration. Read by salvage's capacityFor AND by offline accrual's cap — the reason the capacity upgrade matters.

Purchased hull-pressure rating. Open map, no migration. Written by structures, READ by depth's pressure gate — the one purchasable whose non-inertness is proven against the depth gate rather than against the income rate.
Purchased count of Pearl-only drones (priced in currencies.Pearls). Open map, no migration. NOT wiped by resurface — Pearl purchases are permanent; every other upgrades key is.

The unlocked trench tier (1..5, plus the VIP trench above 5). This is a purchased LEVEL of a named upgradable, which the seam rule sends to the upgrades map — no migration. Reset to 1 by resurface. Registered so depth (writer) and salvage's valueMultiplier chain (reader) agree.

The 2x Credits gamepass EFFECT flag, granted server-side only. Gamepass effect flags ride the flags map by design — no migration. Read directly off the blob by salvage's rateFor (no service seam, so it cannot race).
The Auto-Collect gamepass effect flag. Read by salvage's tick to empty the smelter automatically. Open map, no migration, never set from a client action.
The VIP-trench gamepass effect flag. Read by depth's gate as a hard prerequisite for the exclusive tier (Err PrereqUnmet without it). Open map, no migration.

The idempotency ledger for dev-product receipts (Credit packs S/M/L, the 30-min 2x boost). Purchase idempotency rides the existing receipts seam by design — no migration. Deliberately NOT in PlayerView (toView strips it).

migrations.why: First because every earn path from batch 0 onward must increment it, so it has to exist before any feature builds. Idempotent seed: only set when absent. For a pre-existing blob there is no historical earn ledger, so seed from math.floor(currencies.Credits or 0); defensively recreate stats if the blob lacks it. MUST stamp schemaVersion = 2.

Build order 1. Seeds plot = { plotId = "", claimedAtUnix = 0 } when absent (empty plotId = holds no plot; the join claim fills it). Idempotent so a re-migrate never evicts a live claim. MUST stamp schemaVersion = 3.
Build order 2. Seeds daily = { streak = 0, lastClaimUnix = 0 } when absent — 0 means never claimed, so the window is open immediately on first join. Idempotent. MUST stamp schemaVersion = 4.

Build order 4. Seeds smelter = { storedCredits = 0, lastTickUnix = 0 } when absent. lastTickUnix = 0 is safe ONLY because SalvageService re-stamps it to now at session load before its first tick (otherwise the first tick would credit ~56 years of accrual, clamped to capacity but still a free full smelter). Idempotent. MUST stamp schemaVersion = 5.
Build order 8. Seeds resurfaces = 0 when absent, preserving any existing value so a re-migrate cannot reset an advanced prestige count. MUST stamp schemaVersion = 6.

Build order 9. Seeds boostExpiresUnix = 0 (no active boost) when absent — an existing player simply starts the new schema unboosted, since none was ever persisted. Idempotent. MUST stamp schemaVersion = 7, and CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION becomes 7 with a self-verifying v1->v7 round-trip test.

sharedServices.name: analytics
sharedServices.purpose: THE single analytics emitter on the ctx.analytics seam: ctx.analytics:emit(event, payload), server-clock stamped, buffered in memory so a Tier-1 spec can assert 'event X fired with payload Y at T' with no Roblox runtime. Declares the taxonomy once (session_start, session_end, loop_completed, currency_earned, currency_spent, progression, purchase) and owns the session_start / session_end lifecycle on PlayerAdded / session release. Every feature emits THROUGH this seam nil-safely — no feature stands up analytics of its own, or the game builds it nine times.

sharedServices.name: economy
sharedServices.purpose: THE single Credits/Pearls mutation helper on the ctx.economy seam, standing up cross-cutting behaviour no feature builder can own because the earn/spend sites live in OTHER features. earn(data, currency, amount, source): applies the balance delta, increments stats.lifetimeCredits FOR CREDITS ONLY (never for Pearls), and emits currency_earned. spend(data, currency, amount, sink): guards with Err(Insufficient) before debiting, never allows a negative balance, and emits currency_spent. Both are PURE transforms designed to be applied inside ONE DataService:update, so a builder cannot forget the lifetime counter, cannot mint by read-then-write across a yield, and cannot double-emit. This is the enforcement point for 'lifetime on all earns, never on spend/reset'.

sharedServices.name: joinretry
sharedServices.purpose: Client framework guard (src/client/framework/JoinRetry.luau) — this scaffold does not have one. Every controller here fetches server state on Start (plot.fetch, salvage.fetch, offline.claim, daily.claim), and all of it exists only after loadSession's yield completes; an unguarded Start() call races that yield and, in the offline case, PERMANENTLY loses the accrual because the autosave then erases the away window. No offline verification rung can see this — it is a T2.7 finding by construction, so the guard ships as framework before any controller is written.

sharedServices.name: hudroot
sharedServices.purpose: AMENDMENT A10d: the ONE shared client HUD root — a single ScreenGui plus a simple anchored slot layout every controller mounts into — standing beside JoinRetry in src/client/framework/. Seven feature controllers each say "client controller" and none owned a shared root; without this the merge produces seven overlapping full-screen GUIs, and a pile of stacked panels is the first thing the human sees. Each controller mounts its panel into a NAMED SLOT; no controller creates its own ScreenGui.

retrofits.change: Replace the fresh-player seed `currencies = { Stardust = 0 }` with `currencies = { Credits = 0, Pearls = 0 }`; add default() seeds for plot, smelter, daily, resurfaces, boostExpiresUnix and stats.lifetimeCredits at CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION; append the six ordered steps [1]..[6], each idempotent and each STAMPING its target version.
retrofits.why: The scaffold ships collect-sim's currency. Left alone, Deep Reach mints Stardust while every Credits read starts nil, and the default() seed is a SEPARATE code site from the migrate() steps — seeding one without the other is the classic half-migration.

retrofits.change: Add plot, smelter, daily, resurfaces, boostExpiresUnix to PlayerData and stats.lifetimeCredits inside the stats record; mirror the five top-level fields in PlayerView and add one allowlist line each in toView (stats is copied wholesale, so lifetimeCredits needs no line); bump CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION from 1 to 7. AMENDMENT A4: ALSO widen PlayerView.stats to { playtimeSeconds: number, joinCount: number, lifetimeCredits: number } — toView copying stats wholesale delivers the VALUE but not the TYPE, and PlayerView.stats is a narrow fixed record at Types.luau:48.
retrofits.why: toView is an allowlist — a new PlayerData field is invisible to the client unless added deliberately, so a missing line ships a HUD that renders nil.

retrofits.change: Add the 13 Net.Actions keys; AND extend the exported ActionContext type with the new nil-safe seams `economy: any?, plot: any?, salvage: any?, depth: any?` alongside the existing security/flags/analytics/monetization.

retrofits.change: Add Insufficient, OnCooldown, PrereqUnmet and Unavailable to Result.Codes.
retrofits.why: This scaffold genuinely lacks Insufficient and OnCooldown (they exist only in collect-sim), and every spend/cooldown path in the plan returns one of them.

retrofits.why: Mocks.net today drops any seam it does not name, so a handler reading ctx.economy would see nil in every feature test and the tests would pass against a no-op. The playerData helper stops nine builders hand-writing nine drifting v7 blobs.

retrofits.change: Retarget every `currencies.Stardust` assertion to `currencies.Credits`; update the fresh-default assertions to the v7 shape.
retrofits.why: Inherited collect-sim assertions; the gauntlet must be green BEFORE fan-out or every builder inherits a red baseline and cannot tell its own breakage from the scaffold's.

retrofits.change: Retarget the `currencies.Stardust` sites (including the raw `d.Stardust` single-writer cases) to Credits, and the hard-coded `schemaVersion = 1` seed blobs to the current version.
retrofits.why: Same inherited-currency problem; this is also the spec the integration gate's shared-balance race extends, so it must speak Credits.

retrofits.change: Retarget the Stardust assertions to Credits and extend the round-trip cases to v1->v7 across all six new steps, asserting each step is idempotent and stamps its version.
retrofits.why: Six steps land at once in the contract pass; without a per-step round-trip the 'no step registered' non-destructive break in Migrations.migrate would silently swallow a missing stamp.

retrofits.change: Deleted by build-game once the first real features land (listed here for blast-radius completeness, not as contract-pass work).
retrofits.why: SampleAction writes `currencies.Stardust` directly — if it survives past batch 0 it mints a currency this game does not have, straight past the economy's single-writer path.

retrofits.change: AMENDMENT A10a: DELETE the sample service AND src/client/controllers/sample/, tests/unit/sample.spec.luau, and the Net.Actions.Sample key, IN THIS PASS (the plan had deferred this to later build-game work). Then remove ./unit/sample.spec from tests/run.luau SPEC_PATHS.
retrofits.why: SampleAction writes currencies.Stardust directly and is client-callable. Left alive through batch 0 it mints a currency this game does not have into live blobs, straight past the economy single-writer path; and deleting Net.Actions.Sample later would be a SECOND shared-contract edit outside this guarded pass. Nothing depends on it, and the sample-removal finalization gate would refuse the handoff for it anyway.

retrofits.change: AMENDMENT A10b: pin the PlayerRemoving hook ORDER explicitly, with a comment saying why: AnalyticsService session_end (needs the still-loaded blob) -> PlotService release (frees the dome) -> DataService session release (invalidates the blob).
retrofits.why: Three features hook the same event and nobody owned the ordering. A session_end emitted AFTER the data-layer release reads NoData, so the event fires with an empty payload and the analytics success criterion passes vacuously. features.name: plot
features.specSlice:
FEATURE (verbatim): "**Plot ownership** — claim a free dome on join, persist which plot, release cleanly on leave, and refuse a second claim. *(contract-defining; built in the serial contract pass + first.)*"

CORE LOOP, step 1 (verbatim): "Join → a free dome plot is claimed for you at Depth 1 and its pad lights up."

ART POSTURE (verbatim, the portion you own): "100% greybox-in-code for v1: domes = Parts + transparency ... No external assets in v1." You build the dome plots and their pads. (Drones/conveyors/smelter belong to Salvage core; the stacked trench shells at descending Y belong to Depth tiers.)

WHAT THIS SLICE OWNS
- A per-SERVER plot registry built at boot: a fixed set of dome plots, each free or held by exactly ONE UserId. Exclusivity is enforced entirely server-side.
- Claim on join: once the session's data has loaded, claim the first free plot, persist its id into PlayerData.plot ({ plotId, claimedAtUnix }, server clock), and light its pad. Claiming is idempotent within a session.
- Refuse a second claim: plot.claim from a player who already holds one returns Err(AlreadyClaimed) — NOT Err(Rejected), which this spine already uses for the panic flag (Net.luau:152), and which would make "a second claim is refused" indistinguishable from "the server is panicked". plot.claim when every plot is held returns Err(Unavailable). Never two players on one plot; never two plots for one player — including under interleaved and spam-duplicated claims arriving in the same frame.
- Release on leave: on PlayerRemoving / session release the plot is freed and is immediately re-claimable by the NEXT player. The leave→claim race must neither leak a plot forever nor hand one plot to two players.
- Rejoin: a returning player re-claims a free plot. A persisted plotId whose plot is already held on THIS server must not be honoured — re-claim a free one and rewrite the field.
- The ctx.plot seam every later feature builds on: plotIdFor(player) -> string?, rootFor(player) -> Instance? (the world root every structure parents under), ownerOf(plotId) -> number?. Salvage core parents the smelter/conveyor/drones under this root; Depth tiers moves this root down the Y axis.
- Actions: `plot.claim` — the payload carries NO plot id (the server picks; a client-named plot IS the plot-claim-hijack exploit) — and `plot.fetch` for the HUD/highlight.
- Client controller: highlight and label the local player's dome. Zero authority. It MUST fetch through the shared JoinRetry guard — a Start()-time fetch races loadSession's yield.

NOT THIS SLICE: income of any kind, drones, the conveyor, the smelter (Salvage core); descending the dome (Depth tiers); any currency mutation whatsoever.

PERSISTENCE: `plot: { plotId: string, claimedAtUnix: number }` at schema v2->v3. The contract pass writes the Types field, the migration step, the default seed and the toView line — you only read/write the field through DataService:update.

ORCHESTRATOR AMENDMENT A1 (resolves an overlap the plan left unowned). PLACEMENT AT THE PERSISTED TIER IS YOURS. You place the dome root at claim time — on a FIRST claim AND on every rejoin — at the Y of the player's PERSISTED tier, by reading the nil-safe seam `ctx.depth:tierYFor(data) -> number` (when Depth tiers is not yet built the seam is absent and you default to tier 1's Y, which is exactly the fresh-player case). A returning player whose persisted tier is 4 must find their dome at tier 4's Y on join, NOT at Depth 1. Depth tiers owns MOVING the root on a successful descend; you own where it STARTS. The authoritative fact is the persisted tier; the world position is derived from it, never the reverse.
successCriteria: **Plot ownership is exclusive and released** — a player gets exactly one plot; a second claim is refused; the plot is freed on leave and re-claimable by the next player (test covers rejoin and the leave→claim race).
**No open exploit** — adversarial pass clean (salvage-rate spoof, plot-claim hijack, offline-time forgery, depth-gate bypass, receipt replay).
**Gauntlet green** — stylua · selene · rojo · lune + reachability; per-feature + integration gates green.
features.seamRationale: CLASS-B for the NEW field `plot: { plotId: string, claimedAtUnix: number }`. This is a per-player OWNED-SLOT IDENTITY paired with a server-clock stamp, and no open seam can carry it: currencies holds numbers keyed by currency, flags holds booleans, upgrades holds purchased LEVELS as numbers (and is enumerated by structures.fetch, so a plot id parked there would render as a purchasable), receipts is a boolean idempotency ledger, and timestamps is a fixed record of the session lifecycle, not of world ownership. A string identity + timestamp record is exactly the 'structured record the maps cannot express' case, and the steering names per-player owned-plot identity as class-B outright.

features.name: daily
features.specSlice:
FEATURE (verbatim): "**Daily supply drop** — claim cooldown, streak counter, HUD badge."

RE-ENTRY HOOK (verbatim): "**Daily supply drop**: escalating reward on a 20-22h claim window + HUD badge."

ECONOMY (verbatim, the source line you own): "Sources: drone salvage (rate scales with depth tier), offline accrual, daily supply drop."

WHAT THIS SLICE OWNS
- The `daily.claim` action: server-clock gated. Refuse with Err(OnCooldown) until the window opens; grant on a valid claim; never trust any client-supplied time (the payload carries no timestamp at all).
- The 20-22h claim window, evaluated ONLY against ctx.clock:unix() and the persisted daily.lastClaimUnix. The claim opens once 20h have elapsed since the last claim. A claim made while the window is open continues the streak (streak += 1); a player who lets the window lapse comes back to a reset streak (streak = 1). Both bounds are server-derived constants in your module — the client never sends or influences them.
- The escalating reward: Credits granted as a server-derived function of the streak, with a documented cap so an unbounded streak cannot mint an unbounded balance. Grant through ctx.economy:earn (which increments stats.lifetimeCredits and emits currency_earned) inside ONE DataService:update.
- Concurrency: two claims in the same frame must grant exactly once — the window check and the lastClaimUnix stamp happen in the same lock-held transform, never read-then-write across a yield.
- Client: the HUD badge showing streak and time-until-next-claim, driven from the replicated PlayerView (daily rides toView). It must fetch/subscribe through the shared JoinRetry guard.

NOT THIS SLICE: offline accrual (a separate re-entry hook, owned by Offline accrual); the daily rich wreck / restock (owned by Depth tiers — it is a per-tier salvage-value multiplier, not a claimable reward); any structure or depth purchase.

PERSISTENCE: `daily: { streak: number, lastClaimUnix: number }` at schema v3->v4, written by the contract pass. lastClaimUnix is SERVER unix time.
successCriteria: **Re-entry hooks work** — offline accrual is capped by smelter capacity and claimed on join **without racing session load**; the daily drop claims in a 20–22h window with the HUD badge; the rich wreck resets — all on server time.
**Core analytics events fire** — `session_start`/`session_end`, `loop_completed`, `currency_earned` (smelt), `currency_spent` (structure), `progression` (depth unlock / resurface), `purchase`.
**Gauntlet green** — stylua · selene · rojo · lune + reachability; per-feature + integration gates green.
features.seamRationale: CLASS-B for the NEW field `daily: { streak: number, lastClaimUnix: number }`. flags is boolean-only and cannot hold a streak or a unix stamp. The upgrades map is {[string]: number} and could PHYSICALLY hold two numbers, but it is the shop's purchased-level map: structures.fetch enumerates its keys, so `upgrades.dailyLastClaimUnix` would surface in the shop UI as an upgrade sitting at level 1754400000 and be offered for purchase — a real correctness failure, not a style objection. currencies would make the streak spendable. A fixed-shape streak+timestamp record with its own migration step is the only honest home.

features.name: leaderboard
features.specSlice:
FEATURE (verbatim): "**Leaderboard** — top players by lifetime Credits (in-world GUI)."

WHAT THIS SLICE OWNS
- A ranked snapshot of the players currently on this server, ordered by `stats.lifetimeCredits` descending, top-N (N a server constant), rebuilt on a server-clock cadence and pushed/served to clients.
- The `leaderboard.fetch` action returning that snapshot.
- The in-world GUI board: a greybox Part with a SurfaceGui listing rank, player name and lifetime Credits. Greybox-in-code, no external assets.
- Names: use only the Roblox-provided Name/DisplayName. Do NOT render any player-authored free text — this feature has no text input and must not add one (rule 9).
- Client controller: renders the board and refreshes it; fetches through the shared JoinRetry guard.

CRITICAL — YOU ONLY READ. `stats.lifetimeCredits` is provided by the SERIAL contract pass and is incremented by EconomyService on every earn path, all of which live in other features (salvage, offline, daily, monetization). You must not increment it, must not compute it from a balance, and must not require or depend on any other feature's service. Read the field off the loaded player data through the data layer.

SCOPE FENCE: v1 is SERVER-LOCAL ranking. A cross-server global board (OrderedDataStore) is explicitly OUT of v1 scope — do not add DataStore calls outside `src/server/data/`.

NOT THIS SLICE: producing, incrementing or resetting lifetimeCredits; any currency mutation; any purchase.

PERSISTENCE: none of your own. Append-only: one Net action, zero schema change.
successCriteria: **Gauntlet green** — stylua · selene · rojo · lune + reachability; per-feature + integration gates green.
features.seamRationale: APPEND-ONLY: adds exactly one Net.Actions key (`leaderboard.fetch`) and persists nothing. Its ranking key `stats.lifetimeCredits` is a cross-cutting counter produced by EVERY earn path, so the contract pass owns both the field and its migration — which is precisely why this feature has NO dependsOn on the earn-path features and no false coupling to services it would otherwise have had to wait for.

features.name: salvage
features.specSlice:
FEATURE (verbatim): "**Salvage core** — drones, the conveyor path, and the smelter converting fragments → Credits on a server-authoritative tick. *(contract-defining; built with plot ownership.)*"

CORE LOOP (verbatim, steps 2-3): "Buy a **salvage drone** (dropper) → it hauls wreck fragments along your conveyor to the smelter." / "The smelter converts fragments → **Credits**, continuously, while you stand there or not."

ECONOMY (verbatim): "Currencies: **Credits** (soft, primary)..." / "Sources: drone salvage (rate scales with depth tier)..."

ART POSTURE (verbatim, the portion you own): "drones = small Parts on TweenService paths, conveyors/smelter = Parts. No external assets in v1."

WHAT THIS SLICE OWNS
1. THE TICK — and it is the ONLY tick loop in this game. One server-wide loop (a single task loop over live sessions, never one loop per player), cadence ~1s on the injected server clock. Per session per tick: `stored = math.min(capacityFor(data), stored + rateFor(data) * (now - smelter.lastTickUnix))`, then stamp `smelter.lastTickUnix = now` — all inside ONE DataService:update. It runs whether or not the player is standing there.
2. THE RATE, AS A DERIVED FUNCTION — never a persisted field. Expose `ctx.salvage:rateFor(data) -> creditsPerSecond` and `ctx.salvage:capacityFor(data) -> number`, PURE over the persisted blob and re-evaluated on every tick and every fetch. rateFor reads, in this order: `upgrades.drones` and `upgrades.conveyor` and `upgrades.pearlDrones` (the Structures shop writes them); the permanent prestige multiplier from `data.resurfaces`; the 2x gamepass `data.flags["gamepass.doubleCredits"]` and the 2x boost `now < data.boostExpiresUnix` (both read STRAIGHT OFF THE BLOB, so there is no seam to race); and the per-tier + restock multiplier via the NIL-SAFE seam `ctx.depth` (if ctx.depth ~= nil then ... end). You are built before all of those features: every one of those inputs must be absent-safe and default to a neutral value, AND every one must genuinely reach the returned number, so that when the later features land they change the rate with ZERO edit to this file. A multiplier that is read but never applied is the written-never-read defect this game was written to catch.
3. THE SMELTER — capacity from `upgrades.smelter`; stored output clamped at capacity every tick (a full smelter stops accruing, which is what makes the capacity upgrade matter).
4. COLLECTING — `salvage.collect` moves smelter.storedCredits into currencies.Credits through ctx.economy:earn (which increments stats.lifetimeCredits and emits currency_earned, source="smelt"), zeroing stored in the SAME transform. Spam-duplicated collects must total exactly the stored amount — the second call finds 0 and returns Err(Insufficient). If `data.flags["gamepass.autoCollect"]` is true, the tick performs the same grant automatically — the SAME code path, not a second one that could skip the lifetime increment.
5. HANDOFF WITH OFFLINE ACCRUAL — the away window [timestamps.lastSeenUnix, now] belongs exclusively to Offline accrual. At session load you MUST stamp `smelter.lastTickUnix = now` BEFORE the first tick, so the online tick never re-counts it (and so a migrated lastTickUnix of 0 cannot credit decades of accrual).
6. THE OBSERVATION SURFACE — `salvage.fetch` returns the DERIVED running rate, stored and capacity. This is the value every later feature's success criterion asserts a delta on.
7. THE WORLD — drones as small Parts on TweenService paths, the conveyor and the smelter as Parts, all parented under `ctx.plot:rootFor(player)`. Visuals are cosmetic: no client input and no client timing may influence the rate (salvage-rate spoof).
8. Client controller: HUD showing rate / stored / capacity and the collect prompt. Fetches through the shared JoinRetry guard.

NOT THIS SLICE: selling upgrades or setting prices (Structures shop); the depth tier value table and the restock rotation (Depth tiers — you consume them through the nil-safe ctx.depth seam); the away-window computation (Offline accrual); granting the gamepass flags (Monetization — you only READ them).

PERSISTENCE: `smelter: { storedCredits: number, lastTickUnix: number }` at schema v4->v5, written by the contract pass.

ORCHESTRATOR AMENDMENT A2 (resolves a build-twice overlap). AUTO-COLLECT IS ONE GRANT PATH, NOT TWO. Implement the collect grant ONCE, as a single internal function, and have BOTH `salvage.collect` and the auto-collect tick call it — so the lifetime-counter increment and the currency_earned emit physically cannot be skipped on one of the two triggers. You build this path now, with `flags["gamepass.autoCollect"]` permanently false (Monetization lands later); it must be correct and dormant, not absent. Monetization only SETS that flag — it must never implement a second collect.
successCriteria: **Core loop completable end-to-end** — join → plot claimed → buy drone → smelter yields Credits → buy an upgrade → unlock Depth 2 → resurface for Pearls; an integration test traverses claim→salvage→buy→descend→resurface and emits `loop_completed`.
**Economy is concurrency-safe** — interleaved / spam-duplicated buy + descend + resurface never double-spend Credits or dupe Pearls (race test on the shared balance).
**Core analytics events fire** — `session_start`/`session_end`, `loop_completed`, `currency_earned` (smelt), `currency_spent` (structure), `progression` (depth unlock / resurface), `purchase`.
**No open exploit** — adversarial pass clean (salvage-rate spoof, plot-claim hijack, offline-time forgery, depth-gate bypass, receipt replay).
**Gauntlet green** — stylua · selene · rojo · lune + reachability; per-feature + integration gates green.
features.seamRationale: CLASS-B for the NEW field `smelter: { storedCredits: number, lastTickUnix: number }`, for two independent reasons. (1) storedCredits is UN-BANKED output, not a currency: it must never appear in the HUD's currency row, never be debitable by a purchase, and never be spendable — parking it in the open currencies map would corrupt the meaning of the shared Credits balance the whole economy races on. (2) lastTickUnix must be a stamp DISTINCT from timestamps.lastSeenUnix: the data layer re-stamps lastSeenUnix on every autosave, so reusing it as the online tick base would silently zero the accrual window every 60s — the known offline-base re-stamping defect class. The upgrades map could physically hold two numbers, but it is the shop's purchased-level map and is enumerated by structures.fetch. The income RATE itself is deliberately NOT persisted — it is a server-derived function of the blob, which is what makes 'purchased structures actually change the income rate' assertable as a delta on a running value.

features.name: structures
features.specSlice:
FEATURE (verbatim): "**Structures shop** — server-validated purchases (drone count, conveyor speed, smelter capacity, hull rating); each purchase persisted **and reflected in the running income rate**; shop UI."

CORE LOOP (verbatim, step 4): "Spend Credits on more drones / a faster conveyor / a bigger smelter → income rises."

ECONOMY (verbatim): "Sinks: drones, conveyor speed, smelter capacity, hull-pressure rating, depth unlocks, resurface." (You own drones, conveyor speed, smelter capacity and hull rating. Depth unlocks belong to Depth tiers; resurface belongs to Resurface/prestige.)

LONG GAME (verbatim, the portion you own): "...**resurface** → Pearls → permanent income multipliers + **Pearl-only drones**." You own the Pearl-only drone CATALOG ENTRY (priced in currencies.Pearls). Resurface owns minting Pearls and the permanent multiplier.

WHAT THIS SLICE OWNS
- THE CATALOG, server-owned: `drones` (count), `conveyor` (speed level), `smelter` (capacity level), `hull` (pressure rating) — all priced in Credits — and `pearlDrones`, priced in Pearls. Prices are a server-derived cost curve with a max level; the client NEVER sends a price, only a catalog key.
- `structures.buy`: validate type + range + rate + that the key is in the catalog, then in ONE DataService:update read the level, derive the cost, debit through ctx.economy:spend (Err(Insufficient) if short, never a negative balance, emits currency_spent) and write `upgrades.<key> += 1`. Never read-then-write across a yield. Spam-duplicated and interleaved buys must never double-spend or grant two levels for one debit.
- `structures.fetch`: the catalog with server-derived NEXT-LEVEL prices plus this player's levels, so the shop UI holds no price constants of its own.
- NO PURCHASABLE SHIPS INERT. Each catalog entry must be proven by a DELTA ON A RUNNING SERVER-DERIVED VALUE, not by a persisted field changing: `drones`, `conveyor` and `pearlDrones` must each measurably raise the value `ctx.salvage:rateFor` returns; `smelter` must measurably raise `ctx.salvage:capacityFor` (and therefore the offline cap); `hull` must measurably change the outcome of the Depth pressure gate (it does not touch income — that is its whole point, and it is still forbidden to ship inert).
- The shop UI: a greybox in-world kiosk plus a client panel listing entries, server-fetched prices, owned levels and affordability. Fetches through the shared JoinRetry guard. No client-side price or level authority.

NOT THIS SLICE: the income rate function or the tick (Salvage core owns both — you write the upgrades keys it reads); the depth unlock cost or gate (Depth tiers); minting Pearls or the prestige multiplier (Resurface); gamepass or dev-product purchases (Monetization).

CANONICAL KEYS (registered by the contract pass so parallel features agree): upgrades.drones, upgrades.conveyor, upgrades.smelter, upgrades.hull, upgrades.pearlDrones. Note that resurface wipes every one of these EXCEPT upgrades.pearlDrones.
successCriteria: **Purchased structures actually change the income rate** — every purchasable is asserted by a **delta on the running rate**, not by a persisted field changing. *(This is the written-never-read pattern that produced 26 of collect-sim's 66 defects — no purchasable ships inert.)*
**Economy is concurrency-safe** — interleaved / spam-duplicated buy + descend + resurface never double-spend Credits or dupe Pearls (race test on the shared balance).
**Core analytics events fire** — `session_start`/`session_end`, `loop_completed`, `currency_earned` (smelt), `currency_spent` (structure), `progression` (depth unlock / resurface), `purchase`.
**Gauntlet green** — stylua · selene · rojo · lune + reachability; per-feature + integration gates green.
features.seamRationale: APPEND-ONLY. Every purchasable is a purchased LEVEL/COUNT of a named upgradable, which is exactly what the OPEN `upgrades: { [string]: number }` map exists for — five new keys, zero schema change, zero migration. Costs are debited from the OPEN currencies map (Credits, and Pearls for the Pearl-only drones — a currency key, also no migration). The only shared writes are two Net.Actions keys and the Insufficient result code, both written once by the contract pass.

features.name: depth
features.specSlice:
FEATURE (verbatim): "**Depth tiers** — 5 trench tiers gated by Credits **and** hull rating; the dome visibly descends; per-tier salvage value."

CORE LOOP (verbatim, step 5, the portion you own): "Buy the **Depth unlock** → the whole dome descends to a richer trench tier → repeat →" (the resurface half of that line belongs to Resurface/prestige.)

PROGRESSION (verbatim): "Long game: 5 depth tiers..." and "**Pressure gate:** each depth tier requires a minimum hull rating, so depth cannot be bought purely with income — it needs the upgrade *and* the Credits. (This is the one rule that stops a rich player skipping the middle game.)"

RE-ENTRY HOOK YOU OWN (verbatim): "**Restock**: a daily **rich wreck** that spawns in one trench tier and resets each day." It is assigned here — not to the daily drop — because it "spawns in one trench tier" and its effect IS a per-tier salvage-value multiplier, the responsibility this feature already owns; putting it elsewhere would split the per-tier value across two features and add a second multiplier seam to Salvage core.

MONETIZATION YOU READ (verbatim, the portion you own the EFFECT of): "**VIP trench** (an exclusive depth tier)." You gate that tier on `data.flags["gamepass.vipTrench"]`; Monetization grants the flag.

ART POSTURE (verbatim, the portion you own): "trench tiers = stacked Part shells at descending Y."

WHAT THIS SLICE OWNS
- The 5-tier table (plus the VIP trench above them): per tier, a Credits cost, a minimum hull rating, and a salvage-value multiplier.
- THE PRESSURE GATE, and it must not be bypassable by re-ordering purchases. `depth.descend` validates ALL of the following against the SAME lock-held snapshot in which it debits: (a) the previous tier is already unlocked — tiers are strictly sequential, so no tier can be skipped by any purchase order; (b) `upgrades.hull >= HULL_MIN[nextTier]` -> Err(PrereqUnmet) if not; (c) enough Credits -> Err(Insufficient) if not; and for the VIP trench (d) flags["gamepass.vipTrench"] -> Err(PrereqUnmet) if absent. Buying hull first, Credits first, or spamming descend must all converge on this one guarded transform. Writes `upgrades.depth = nextTier`, debits via ctx.economy:spend (emits currency_spent), emits `progression`, and emits `loop_completed` on the FIRST successful descend of a session (the terminal step of the spec's core loop).
- THE SEAM SALVAGE CORE READS: `ctx.depth:valueMultiplier(data, nowUnix) -> number` — the per-tier salvage multiplier for `upgrades.depth`, MULTIPLIED by today's restock bonus when the player's current tier is today's restock tier. Salvage core reads this nil-safely and was built before you; landing this seam is what must produce a measurable delta on the running rate.
- THE RESTOCK ROTATION: a day index derived from ctx.clock:unix() ONLY, deterministically selecting one trench tier per server-day, resetting each day. No client input, no os.time, no client-supplied day.
- `depth.fetch`: current tier, the next tier's Credits + hull requirement, and today's restock tier (for the HUD badge).
- THE VISIBLE DESCENT: move the player's plot root — `ctx.plot:rootFor(player)` — down the Y axis to the tier's shell, and build the stacked trench shells as greybox Parts. Progression must be legible from across the map. The descent is cosmetic-follows-state: the authoritative fact is `upgrades.depth`, and the world position is derived from it (never the other way round).
- Client controller: descend prompt, requirement panel (cost + hull needed + what you have), restock badge. Fetches through the shared JoinRetry guard. No client authority over the gate.

NOT THIS SLICE: selling hull rating (Structures shop writes upgrades.hull; you only read it); the income tick or the rate function (Salvage core — you supply one multiplier into it); granting the VIP gamepass flag (Monetization); resetting the tier on prestige (Resurface writes upgrades.depth back to 1).

ORCHESTRATOR AMENDMENT A1 (resolves an overlap the plan left unowned). You PROVIDE `ctx.depth:tierYFor(data) -> number` (the world Y for the player's persisted tier), which PlotService reads at claim time so a returning player's dome is placed at their persisted tier rather than at Depth 1. You MOVE the root only on a successful descend. Between you, every path that positions a dome is owned: claim/rejoin = plot, descend = depth.

features.specSlice:
FEATURE (verbatim): "**Monetization** — gamepass checks (2x / auto-collect / VIP trench) + dev-product receipts."

MONETIZATION (verbatim, in full): "Gamepasses: **2x Credits**, **Auto-Collect** (smelter never needs a manual empty), **VIP trench** (an exclusive depth tier). Ownership is **granted server-side** — checked on join via `UserOwnsGamePassAsync` and on a fresh purchase via `PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished` — and recorded as persisted `flags['gamepass.*']` booleans that gate each effect (never set from a client action)." / "Dev products: Credit packs (S/M/L), a 30-min **2x boost** — **persisted** (the expiry survives a crash/rejoin, not session-only), stamped atomically with the idempotent receipt ledger."

WHAT THIS SLICE OWNS
- GAMEPASS OWNERSHIP, GRANTED SERVER-SIDE ONLY. On join, `MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync` for each of the three passes; on a fresh purchase, `MarketplaceService.PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished`. Write the result into persisted `flags["gamepass.doubleCredits"]`, `flags["gamepass.autoCollect"]`, `flags["gamepass.vipTrench"]`. There is deliberately NO Net action for this — a client-settable gamepass flag is a free gamepass. Emit `purchase` on a false->true transition. Both API calls can throw/yield: pcall them, retry within budget, and never let a failed check clear an already-granted flag.
- THE EFFECTS ARE READ BY OTHER FEATURES, and your gate must prove each one actually lands: `doubleCredits` and the boost multiply the value `ctx.salvage:rateFor` returns; `autoCollect` makes Salvage core's tick empty the smelter with no manual collect; `vipTrench` is what lets Depth tiers enter the exclusive tier (Err(PrereqUnmet) without it). Assert each as a DELTA on the running rate / on the gate outcome — a flag written and never read is the exact defect class this game is graded against.
- DEV PRODUCTS via `MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt`, IDEMPOTENTLY: Credit packs S/M/L (grant Credits through ctx.economy:earn, which increments stats.lifetimeCredits and emits currency_earned) and the 30-min 2x boost (set `boostExpiresUnix = ctx.clock:unix() + 1800`, EXTENDING from the later of now and the current expiry so a stacked purchase is never silently swallowed). The receipt id is recorded in the `receipts` ledger and the grant is applied in the SAME DataService:update — an already-present receipt id grants nothing and returns PurchaseGranted; ANY failure returns `Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet`. Replaying the same receipt must never double-grant. Emit `purchase` after the grant commits.
- REAL MONEY GUARD: if `ctx.persistenceDegraded` is true (the server fell back to the in-memory store — the field already exists in Context.build), a successful save is NOT durability. Do not acknowledge a receipt as processed; return NotProcessedYet so Roblox re-delivers it to a healthy server.
- THE BOOST IS PERSISTED: `boostExpiresUnix` survives a crash/rejoin. Salvage core reads `now < data.boostExpiresUnix` straight off the blob, so there is no session-only state to lose and no seam to race.
- Client: purchase prompts (client-initiated MarketplaceService prompts are fine — the GRANT is server-side) and a HUD boost-remaining timer driven from the replicated PlayerView. Fetches through the shared JoinRetry guard.

NOT THIS SLICE: the rate formula or the smelter tick (Salvage core reads your flags); the depth gate (Depth tiers reads your VIP flag); the shop's Credits-priced catalog (Structures shop).

features.seamRationale: MOSTLY seams, but CLASS-B for one field. The gamepass EFFECT booleans ride the open `flags` map (exactly what the steering says gamepass-effect flags are for) and purchase idempotency rides the open `receipts` ledger — neither needs a migration. A top-level number with its own migration step, its own toView line, and a v1->v7 round-trip test.
